ideas.description: Start from A1a (E001 tip) and add progressive resizing with a long full-res tail. Total 9.0 epochs (LR/EMA/lookahead schedules rescaled to the step count as the recipe already does). Train at 26 px for steps 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60% and 32 px for the last 40%. Low-res batches are made by applying the existing flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True) to 26/28 px. No random-resized crop. The final group pool must still end at 3x3 (26->25->12->6->3, 28->27->13->6->3). In build, compile and warm up all 3 train shapes plus eval at 32 px, so nothing recompiles in timed code. Instrumentation only: log a hash of the first batch's augmentation parameters per trial.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.3-6.5 s, -10 to -13% vs A1a's 7.22 s. Per-epoch costs from E006: 26 px ~0.56, 28 px ~0.65, 32 px ~0.84 s. Accuracy 0.751-0.757: E006 lost 0.69 pp with only 2 full-res epochs and a degenerate 24 px stage; this has 3.6 full-res epochs. If >=0.753 it becomes the new tip. If 0.749-0.753, follow with 9.5 epochs and the same fractions (about +0.35 s).

ideas.description: Take E006's schedule unchanged: 9.0 epochs, epochs 0-3 low-res, 4-6 at 28 px, 7-8 at 32 px. Make exactly two changes, which together are the H2.5 confound removal: (a) the first phase uses 26 px instead of 24 px, and (b) replace random-resized crop with flip + translate-2 at 32 px followed by an antialiased bilinear downsample to the phase resolution. Warm up all shapes in build.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.1-6.3 s, +4-6% vs E006's 5.88 s, since the 26 px epochs cost ~0.56 s vs 0.47 s. Accuracy 0.750-0.754, i.e. +0.2 to +0.6 pp over E006's 0.748. A gain of >=0.4 pp supports H2.5 (the loss came from confounds, not low resolution). A gain of <0.2 pp means the short full-res tail is the binding factor and favors the H2.1.2 schedule.

ideas.description: On the 8.0-epoch recipe (the E007 control, 0.7502 / 6.80 s), change only the LR schedule's end point: decay linearly to 0 at the last step instead of to 0.07x the peak. Keep warmup, peak LR, the BN-bias multiplier and the lookahead/EMA schedule unchanged. Being zero-cost, the resulting accuracy lever can stack onto any progressive-resizing recipe.
ideas.expected: Time 6.80 s ±1% (unchanged). Accuracy +0.1 to +0.4 pp over the control, giving 0.751-0.754. If >=0.753 it becomes the new tip at about 6.80 s (-5.8%) and the change gets ported to the progressive recipe. A gain under 0.2 pp is within perturbation noise and refutes H6.1.1.

ideas.description: RNG audit for progressive resizing, with no recipe change. Rerun E006's code (commit ed8dc49) adding only logging: per trial, log a hash of the first train batch's augmentation parameters (crop boxes/scales, flip mask, translate offsets) and a hash of the initial model parameters after prepare. Also run seed 0 twice through a side script that calls build/prepare/train in-process. Check the result: augmentation generators must be derived from the trial seed and reset in prepare. If they are not, fix that in every progressive successor. A shared stream would break the no-information-flow and seeding rules.
ideas.expected: Accuracy and time identical to E006 (0.7480, ~5.88 s). Prediction: the hashes differ across seeds 0-2, and repeating seed 0 reproduces them. Then E006's 0.02 pp per-seed spread was chance and H2.1.3 is supported. If the hashes are identical across seeds, or the generator is built in build/import, the progressive line needs a seeding fix and its accuracy numbers need re-measuring.

ideas.description: Take the H2.1.2 recipe (9.0 epochs; 26 px for 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60%, 32 px for the last 40%). Change only how low-res batches are made. Crop mode: after flip + translate-2 at 32 px, take a random 26x26 or 28x28 crop (independent offset per image, done via unfold/gather or a batched index on the GPU), with no rescaling, so object scale matches the test images. Do not use the antialiased downsample. Keep the shapes identical so the compiled graphs are reused.
ideas.expected: Time within ±1% of the H2.1.2 run. Accuracy differs by -0.3 to +0.4 pp. H2.5.2 predicts crop mode wins by >=0.3 pp (FixRes scale argument). If it loses, the network benefits from seeding the full field of view at low res and downsampling is the right operator.

ideas.description: On A1a (8.5 epochs, everything else unchanged), narrow group 2 from 384 to 320 channels, which also shrinks group 3's first conv input. Recompile and warm up in build. Group 2 at 15x15 carries ~50% of conv FLOPs by a rough count. 384->320 cuts total conv FLOPs by about 15%. The exchange rate to beat is the epoch-cut rate, 0.08 pp per 1% of time (E007).
ideas.expected: Time about 6.4-6.7 s (-8 to -12%). Accuracy 0.746-0.752 (-0.3 to -0.8 pp). If the loss per 1% of time saved is <0.06 pp, it beats epoch cuts and is worth combining with +0.5 epochs or with progressive resizing. Otherwise H2.6 is refuted (capacity is not cheap to remove on CIFAR-100).

ideas.description: On E006's code (commit ed8dc49), add only a FixRes-style BN re-estimation at the end of train. After the final EMA/lookahead weights are set, reset the BN running stats and run a forward-only pass in train mode (momentum=None, cumulative average) at 32 px over ~5000 augmented training images (5 batches of 1024, flip + translate only), under no_grad. Warm up this shape in build (it is the existing 32 px train shape).
ideas.expected: Time +0.5 to +1.5% (about 5.92-5.97 s). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.3 pp over E006's 0.748. A small gain is likely because E006 already ended with 2 epochs at 32 px. A gain of >=0.2 pp supports H6.2.1 and makes it a cheap add-on for any schedule with a short full-res tail.

ideas.description: On A1a (8.5 epochs), switch the 3x3 conv filters of the three groups to Muon: lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, Nesterov, 3 Newton-Schulz steps in bf16, filters reshaped to [out, in*9]. Keep SGD-Nesterov with the existing hyperparameters for BN params, biases and the head. Keep the LR schedule shape and the lookahead/EMA. Warm up the compiled NS step in build. This is an explore run on the one optimization-efficiency lever not yet tried; E008 suggests the short schedule is under-fitting.
ideas.expected: Time +1 to +4% (7.3-7.5 s), from NS matmuls on small matrices. Accuracy 0.750-0.757. H5.1.1 predicts no gain over SGD of more than 0.2 pp. A gain of >=0.4 pp would refute H5 and justify a Muon run at 8.0 epochs or on the progressive recipe.

structured_output.summary: The open lever is clear by now. E004, E010 and E011 settled that the GPU is energy-bound, so overhead cuts don't move time. E003, E005, E008 and E009 settled that regularization and capacity tweaks don't help. Progressive resizing (E006) has the best exchange rate: -0.69 pp for -18.6% time, about 2x better than cutting full-res epochs (E007). The top priority is to turn that into a feasible tip. H2.1.2 (P5) is a 9-epoch 26/28/32 schedule with a 40% full-res tail and antialiased downsampling, predicted at about 6.3-6.5 s and 0.751-0.757. H2.5.1 (P4) removes E006's two confounds (24 px pool geometry and random-resized crop) at E006's fractions. H2.5.2 (P3) compares crop mode with resize mode on the H2.1.2 schedule. H6.1.1 (P4) tests a zero-cost LR-to-zero decay on the 8.0-epoch control, which could be a direct tip at 6.80 s and would stack onto resizing. Diagnostics and explores: an RNG/seeding audit of E006's suspiciously tight 0.02 pp per-seed spread (H2.1.3, which also checks rule compliance), narrowing group 2 as an architectural FLOP cut (H2.6.1), FixRes BN re-estimation (H6.2.1) and Muon (H5.1.1). With I013 still running, 8 ideas are now queued. Nothing is dropped, because every queued hypothesis is still open.
